summary: The MAJOR is genuinely fixed and I verified it independently rather than accepting the numbers: reproducing the pre-M4.9 walk in my own tree (crossFromCheckpoint short-circuited to false, no probe issued) gives totals 29/46/80/148/284 at 1/2/4/8/16 prior terms, GETs 18/33/63/123/243, LISTs 3/4/6/10/18, stats 4/5/7/11/19; the staged tree gives 17 flat with GETs 5, LISTs 3, stats 5. That matches ADR-0035's new table, the backlog row and the test class javadoc exactly, and the cited before-tree `15da3fb` is M4.8c, the commit immediately before this one. The ADR's corrected rejected-alternative evidence also checks out: under `if (chainEpoch == ownEpoch) return false;` exactly `aCheckpointSittingEXACTLYOnTheBarrierIsUsed` and `aTakeoverReadsEveryEntryOfEveryANCESTORAndTHATISAREGRESSION` fail, and `recoveringAChainThatCheckpointedItsOWNProgressKeepsItsNextSequence` passes, as the ADR now says. The `rounds:M4.9` argument's load-bearing claim also holds: I traced the cumulativeness induction to `CheckpointWriter.capture` reading `log.offsets()` and `CommitLog.open` merging `ChainReplay.inherited(...)` into `nextOffsets`, so no checkpoint can predate what its writer inherited. Two things the fixes did not close. First, the new burned-epoch test proves narrower than its name: it pins that the checkpoint is READ, not that the walk STOPS, and the cost mutant that separates them survives the whole build with a per-entry crossing restored. Second, the retracted before-series survives at two live sites the correction did not grep for, one of them production source under the word `measured`.

findings.title: aRunOfBURNEDEpochsStillStopsAtTheCheckpointBehindThem pins that the checkpoint is READ, not that the walk STOPS -- and the mutant that separates them restores a per-entry crossing while the whole build stays green
findings.mutation: In ChainReplay.replayAncestry's `neverOpened` branch, replace `if (chainEpoch >= 1 && crossFromCheckpoint(hops, chainEpoch, limit)) { break; }` with `if (chainEpoch >= 1) { crossFromCheckpoint(hops, chainEpoch, limit); }` -- cross, take the checkpoint's offsets, then keep walking and add the full Hop(chainEpoch, 0, limit) anyway.
findings.failure_scenario: MEASURED IN MY OWN TREE, not argued. Under that mutant `./gradlew test` is BUILD SUCCESSFUL across every module, and the new test passes unchanged, because the fixture's checkpoint claims 500 while the deltas only reach 4 and `fold` merges with `Math::max` -- so a walk that replays epoch 1 in full past the checkpoint produces the identical 500. What the mutant does change is the only thing the test's own name asserts. Instrumenting the same fixture through CountingBinStore: staged tree 3 GETs / 3 LISTs / 5 stats at 4 deltas AND at 40 deltas (flat); mutant 9 GETs at 4 deltas and 45 at 40 -- one GET per entry of the ancestor, plus an extra LIST. That is the unbounded crossing M4.9 exists to remove, on the burned-epoch path this test was added to cover, and nothing catches it. The `.as()` label says the walk `STOPPED at epoch 1's checkpoint, rather than replaying its deltas past it`; replaying its deltas past it is precisely what is not constrained. This is the shape M4.8c's own row already records once -- an `.as()` label claiming coverage that did not exist -- and the choice of a checkpoint claiming MORE than the deltas is what makes stopping unobservable, since `Math::max` absorbs anything the extra hop reads. Fix by asserting through CountingBinStore that the count is flat in the ancestor's chain length (4 vs 40 deltas), or by narrowing the name and the label to what is actually pinned: the probe is issued and its answer used. Deleting the probe outright IS killed by this test -- I measured that too -- so half the round-2 minor is genuinely closed.

findings.title: The retracted 26/43/77/145/281 series still stands at two live sites the correction did not grep for -- one of them production source, and misattributed
findings.rule: non-negotiable 4 (never claim a number was measured without having measured it)
findings.failure_scenario: ChainReplay.java:161, inside the comment that justifies the checkpoint termination: `which M4.6e measured growing 26/43/77/145/281 requests at 1/2/4/8/16 prior terms.` And LocalSequencerBoundedRecoveryTest.java:86: `// Before this change: 26 requests at 1 prior term, 281 at 16.` -- 34 lines below the paragraph in the SAME FILE that now says those exact numbers `describe an older tree` and were `Re-measured here rather than carried forward`. The file contradicts itself, and the production comment asserts the retracted series with no annotation at all. I measured the real series myself: 29/46/80/148/284. The attribution is wrong too: M4.6e's own backlog-done row does not carry that table, it says `M4.9's row now carries the measured table`, so `M4.6e measured` names a measurement M4.6e never made. Failure scenario, and it is the round-2 major relocated rather than closed: the next session touching bounded recovery greps for the before-state, finds 26/281 in `main/` and in the cost test, finds 29/284 in ADR-0035 and the backlog row, and cannot tell which is the older tree without re-measuring -- exactly the state the round-2 finding described, and exactly the `WHEN A MUTANT IS FOUND, FIND EVERY SITE OF ITS SHAPE` lesson this task's own row records twice (M4.8c round 3 was the same defect: a retracted sentence left standing in a test file). The remedy is two comment lines, not a split. NOT filed: backlog-notes.md:173 still carries `1 prior term 17/26 ... 16 terms 242/281` under the word MEASURED, but done rows keep their specification notes verbatim by convention (M4.8a/b/b1/b2/c all do), and both the done row and the ADR annotate the origin.

findings.title: The fix for the half-done split deleted takeoverCost's javadoc as well as the duplicated fixture, taking the `K IS INJECTED AT 1` warning out of the tree entirely
findings.failure_scenario: The orphan copy in BoundedRecoveryFixture was correctly removed, but the same block was also removed from LocalSequencerBoundedRecoveryTest, where it was NOT an orphan -- it documented `takeoverCost`, which is still there. Gone with it is the sentence the commit itself treats as load-bearing: `a fixture using the 4-arg start would build an ancestry with NO checkpoints in it and measure the unbounded path while claiming to measure the bounded one`. `takeoverCost` now has no javadoc at all and two bare `noRenew(), 1, frozen()` literals whose `1` is unexplained; a maintainer simplifying to the 4-arg `start` turns both constant-cost assertions into comparisons of two unbounded measurements that happen to be equal, and ADR-0035's `uncheckpointed by construction` argument for LocalSequencerFailoverTest is what makes that easy to do by accident. Re-attach the paragraph to `takeoverCost`. A triple blank line is left at the old site, and the new test in BoundedRecoveryCorrectnessTest has no blank line before its `@Test`.
